To apply for admission to the Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) department at East West University (EWU), you need to meet the following admission requirements:

### Admission Requirements for B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)
1. **General Admission Criteria**: Must meet the general admission criteria of EWU for the Faculty of Sciences and Engineering.
2. **Educational Background**: Applicants should have completed their HSC or equivalent level with a background in Science, including Mathematics.
3. **Admission Test**: Candidates must qualify in the EWU Admission Test. The date of the test is announced in major daily newspapers.
4. **Documentation**: Copies of Marks Certificates/Transcripts, Testimonials of SSC & HSC or “O” & “A” levels must be submitted during admission.
5. **Minimum GPA**: Candidates scoring GPA 5.00 (including the 4th subject) in the immediate past SSC and HSC examinations will be awarded a 50% merit scholarship at entry level in Undergraduate Programs for the first year, subject to qualifying in the EWU Admission Test and maintaining a minimum GPA of 3.50 in each semester as a regular student [Page 176, Source: EWU_Complete_Data_2025_2026.pdf; Page 33, Source: ewuundergraduate-bulletin-14th-edition-doc-version.pdf].

is there any capstone or thesis for cse department?

Yes, the Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) department at East West University (EWU) includes a capstone project as part of its curriculum. Here are the details regarding the capstone project:

### Capstone Project Information
- **Course Code**: CSE400
- **Course Title**: Capstone Project
- **Credits**: 0+6=6
- **Prerequisite**: Students must have completed at least 105 credit hours.

### Course Objectives:
The main objective of the Capstone project is to create a platform for students to gain experience in finding acceptable solutions to practical open-ended Information and Communication Engineering design problems. During this project, students are expected to learn how to manage a project, work in a team, and acquire soft skills.

### Course Contents:
The Capstone project provides students the opportunity to apply and integrate the knowledge and skills gathered through earlier coursework. Students will take primary responsibility to identify, organize, plan, and execute different tasks associated with designing a practical system or component. Students will work on projects in teams.

### Course Outcomes (COs):
After completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Identify and examine various problem domains (literature review); justify and finalize the problem statement; write a project proposal for the capstone project.
2. Perform and complete requirement analysis; outline, justify, and finalize design methodologies for the finalized project.
3. Design hardware and/or software for the finalized project incorporating societal, environmental, and ethical considerations; build the proposed system incorporating project management and financial principles and justify (test) the deliverable system.
4. Use different visualization tools and write and present (oral and/or poster) technical reports incorporating different evaluation matrices including efficiency, cost; and ethical, societal, economic, and environmental impacts.

This information is sourced from the official documents of East West University [Page 40, Source: ewuundergraduate-bulletin-14th-edition-doc-version.pdf; Page 24, Source: ewuundergraduate-bulletin-14th-edition-doc-version.pdf].
